title: Consolidated Terraform module for CloudTrail audit pipeline, OpenSearch ILM, and retention policies
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: deliver a single, opinionated Terraform module that provisions CloudTrail (multi-region) -> encrypted S3 bucket + lifecycle -> OpenSearch ingestion pipeline with index lifecycle management (ILM) and snapshot retention, plus optional Kibana dashboard provisioning. The module must be reusable for Private (VPC) deployment customers, support cross-account logging, and follow Redwood's security/compliance defaults (KMS encryption, MFA delete guardrails where required).

Acceptance criteria:
- Terraform module supports inputs for: trail name, multi-region flag, S3 bucket naming template, kms_key_arn, opensearch_domain_config (size/zone), ilm_policy (hot/warm/cold/retain days), snapshot_repository, cross_account_trust (list), retention_days for S3 and indices.
- Module creates CloudTrail trails with CloudWatch Logs integration and S3 delivery; enables log file validation for integrity checks.
- S3 bucket has lifecycle rules: transition to IA after 30d, Glacier after 180d, delete after configurable (default 3650d) but never less than 90d.
- OpenSearch domain provisioning includes ILM rules, automated snapshots to an S3 snapshot repository, and a daily snapshot lifecycle with retention policy.
- Module emits Terraform output with endpoints, bucket names, role ARNs, and recommended alerting CloudWatch metric names.
- Includes upgrade/migration plan and tests (unit, Terratest) and CI pipeline steps for terraform fmt/tflint/plan validation.
- Health checks: provide scripts/terraform null_resource that runs preflight validations and a periodic Lambda (optional) that checks last delivery time and index freshness.
- Documentation and example usage in module README, plus a sample usage for single-account and cross-account collector setup.
design_notes:
Interface design highlights:
- inputs (strings): name_prefix, region_list (comma-separated), multi_region (true/false), s3_lifecycle_delete_days, kms_key_arn, opensearch_instance_type, opensearch_instance_count, enable_kibana_provisioning (true/false), snapshot_s3_bucket, cross_account_log_delivery_roles (comma-separated).
- outputs (strings): cloudtrail_id, s3_bucket_name, opensearch_endpoint, snapshot_repo_name, delivery_role_arn.
- Resources: aws_cloudtrail, aws_s3_bucket + aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration, aws_kms_key (optional), aws_iam_role for delivery, aws_opensearch_domain, aws_iam_policy_attachment for access, aws_lambda (optional health-check), aws_cloudwatch_event_rule for snapshot schedule.
- Arg validation: prevent retention < 90 days; warn if multi_region true but region_list omitted.

Compatibility notes:
- Keep backward compatibility for existing installs by supporting legacy variable names with deprecated warnings.
- Migration: provide migration script (terraform state mv + tf resource rename recommendations) documented in the README.
- Module versions: semver-major bump policy for breaking changes; provide upgrade guide for v1->v2 that covers index template changes and snapshot repo name changes.
implementation_plan:
Phases:
1) Prototype TF module with CloudTrail -> S3 + basic lifecycle, KMS encryption enabled, and smoke tests (local terratest). (Owner: Marcus)
2) Add OpenSearch domain + ILM policies and automated snapshot wiring to S3. Add integration tests that index a small payload and validate ILM rollover triggers. (Owner: Marcus + infra eng).
3) Add cross-account delivery role and example consumer account setup. Add RBAC notes for Private deployments. (Owner: Aisha)
4) CI: add terraform fmt, tflint, validate, and a terraform plan against a dedicated staging account. Add Terratest into pipeline with GitHub Actions. (Owner: SRE).
5) Documentation, upgrade guide, and handoff to Solutions for customer onboarding.

Milestones and PRs:
- PR # (WIP): github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/412 (prototype)
- PR next: add opensearch-ilm + snapshot: PR 419

Rollback strategy: revert module to previous release, and run migration script to restore prior index templates. For critical infra, follow Redwood oncall runbook to failover to archived OpenSearch domain in another region.
tests_and_ci:
Testing planned:
- Unit: terraform validate + tflint ruleset with custom rules for retention bounds.
- Integration: Terratest that provisions module in a sandbox account, sends sample CloudTrail events, confirms S3 object arrival, checks OpenSearch indexing, and verifies ILM snapshot creation.
- Canary: deploy module in dedicated staging VPC and run periodic health-check lambda for 14 days before promoting.
- CI: GH Actions job: terraform fmt -> tflint -> terraform init -> terraform plan (with var-file), and a blocked merge if plan shows >2 resource changes unless approved.

Health check automation:
- Lambda-based monitor that queries S3 last-modified for trail prefix and checks OpenSearch _cluster/health and index/_stats. Emits CloudWatch metrics: AuditDeliveryLatency, OpenSearchIndexAge. Playbooks for alerts documented in runbook.
- Optional Prometheus exporter for self-hosted monitoring when Private customer provides networking for scraping.
security_and_compliance:
Defaults enforced:
- KMS encryption for all S3 buckets and OpenSearch encryption at rest.
- CloudTrail log file validation enabled.
- Audit IAM roles limited to least-privilege; cross-account roles flagged for manual review.
- Tagging policy: apply tags {Owner, Environment, Compliance:PCI/HIPAA?}.
- Security review required before v1.0 release.
- Data residency: region_list input enforces placement; multi-region trails validated against customer compliance requirements.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: OpenSearch sizing mistakes could lead to high cost or slow ingestion. Mitigation: conservative default instance types and explicit sizing variables; guidance doc for expected events/day.
Risk: Retention policy misconfiguration causing premature deletion. Mitigation: validation guardrails and default minimum retention of 90 days; explicit confirmation step in upgrade plan for reducing retention.
Risk: State migration complexity. Mitigation: helper scripts for terraform state mapping plus scheduled maintenance window documented in upgrade guide.
